content: The references provided are a comprehensive collection of studies, reviews, and reports addressing various aspects of lead exposure, toxicity, and management. 1. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (Second Edition) provides a structured framework for developing evidence-based guidelines, ensuring consistency and quality in health recommendations. This document was accessed on August 31, 2021. 2. Bates and Wiseman conducted a narrative review on gastrointestinal decontamination methods for lead ingestion, highlighting the clinical approaches to managing acute lead exposure. This work was prepared under the auspices of the World Health Organization in 2020. 3. Bates, Tempowski, and Nussbaumer-Streit explored the role of nutritional supplementation in mitigating lead poisoning, emphasizing the potential benefits of dietary interventions. This publication was prepared by the WHO in 2020. 4. Bates, Wiseman, Tempowski, and Nussbaumer-Streit reviewed the use of dimercaprol as a chelating agent for treating lead poisoning, providing insights into its efficacy and clinical application. This WHO-prepared document was published in 2020. 5. The same authors also examined the therapeutic use of penicillamine for lead poisoning, discussing its pharmacological properties and clinical outcomes. This work was prepared by the WHO in 2020. 6. Sodium calcium edetate, another chelating agent, was reviewed by Bates and colleagues for its application in lead poisoning treatment. This WHO-prepared publication was completed in 2020. 7. Succimer, a chelating agent specifically used for lead poisoning, was analyzed by Bates and colleagues, focusing on its clinical utility and safety profile. This work was prepared by the WHO in 2020. 8. Bates authored a narrative review on the use of chelation therapy for treating lead poisoning during pregnancy, addressing the unique challenges and risks associated with this population. This WHO-prepared document was completed in 2020. 9. The WHO Food Additive Series (64) includes a safety evaluation of certain food additives and contaminants, with a focus on lead exposure. This report was part of the 73rd meeting of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives. 10. The National Toxicology Program Monograph on the health effects of low-level lead exposure provides a detailed analysis of the toxicological and epidemiological evidence, accessed on August 31, 2021. 11. The Final Review of Scientific Information on Lead, available through the WHO, compiles extensive data on lead toxicity and its global health implications. This document was accessed on August 31, 2021. 12. The Final Human Health State of the Science Report on Lead provides a comprehensive assessment of lead's impact on human health, accessed on February 1, 2021. 13. Thornton, Rauitiu, and Brush authored Lead: The Facts, a detailed resource published by the International Lead Association in 2001, summarizing the properties, uses, and health risks of lead. 14. The WHO publication Childhood Lead Poisoning provides an in-depth analysis of the sources, health effects, and prevention strategies for lead exposure in children. This document was accessed on July 7, 2021. 15. A WHO press release from August 30, 2021, announced the global elimination of leaded petrol, marking a significant milestone in reducing lead exposure and its associated health risks. 16. Miranda, Anthopolos, and Hastings conducted a geospatial analysis of the effects of aviation gasoline on childhood blood lead levels, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2011. 17. Fewtrell, Kaufmann, and Prüss-Üstün assessed the environmental burden of lead-related diseases at national and local levels, as part of the WHO Environmental Burden of Disease Series. 18. Taylor and Schniering examined public health efforts to minimize risks associated with environmental lead exposure in children, focusing on Mount Isa, Queensland, Australia, published in 2010. 19. Ji and colleagues highlighted the public health crisis of lead poisoning in China due to industrialization, as reported in The Lancet in 2011. 20. Van Geen et al. conducted a national assessment of lead exposure from soil in Peruvian mining towns, supported by contrasting case studies, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2012. 21. Dooyema and colleagues documented an outbreak of fatal childhood lead poisoning linked to artisanal gold mining in Nigeria, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2012. 22. Mathee et al. investigated lead exposure in young schoolchildren from South African subsistence fishing communities, published in Environmental Research in 2013. 23. The WHO publication on recycling used lead-acid batteries discusses the health considerations and risks associated with this practice, accessed on August 31, 2021. 24. The WHO technical brief on the global elimination of lead paint outlines the rationale and strategies for countries to take action against lead-based paints, accessed on August 31, 2021. 25. Weiss et al. studied the distribution of lead in urban roadway grit and its association with elevated steel structures, published in Chemosphere in 2006. 26. Caravanos et al. conducted a two-year survey on leaded dust deposition in New York City, analyzing both exterior and interior environments, published in Environmental Research in 2006. 27. Lucas et al. investigated the sources of lead in residential floor dust and the variability of dust lead loading within homes, published in Science of the Total Environment in 2014. 28. The Integrated Science Assessment for Lead, available through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, provides a detailed evaluation of lead's health effects, accessed on February 1, 2021. 29. The WHO background document on lead in drinking water supports the development of guidelines for drinking water quality, accessed on August 31, 2021. 30. Colling et al. studied the effects of plumbosolvency and its control in hard water systems, published in the Water Environment Journal in 1992. 31. Hayes edited a best practice guide on controlling lead in drinking water, published by IWA Publishing in 2010. 32. Weidenhamer et al. investigated lead exposure from aluminum cookware in Cameroon, published in Science of the Total Environment in 2014. 33. Klein et al. reported on fatal lead poisoning caused by earthenware containers, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1970. 34. Galvez et al. documented childhood lead poisoning from commercially manufactured French ceramic dinnerware in New York City, published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2004. 35. Hellström-Lindberg et al. reported lead poisoning cases linked to souvenir earthenware, published in the International Archives of Occupational and Environmental Health in 2006. 36. Dickinson et al. described a case of lead poisoning in a family due to cocktail glasses, published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1972. 37. Forsyth et al. conducted a case-control study on elevated blood lead levels among pregnant women in rural Bangladesh, published in Environmental Research in 2018. 38. Tamayo y Ortiz et al. studied the relationship between lead in candy and blood lead levels in children in Mexico City, published in Environmental Research in 2016. 39. Arnold and Morgan reported on the management of lead encephalopathy with DMSA after exposure to lead-contaminated moonshine, published in the Journal of Medical Toxicology in 2015. 40. Yabe et al. analyzed metal distribution in tissues of free-range chickens near a lead-zinc mine in Zambia, published in Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry in 2013. 41. Corley and Mutiti studied the accumulation of lead in Chinese cabbage due to lead species and growth time, published in Global Challenges in 2017. 42. Gustavsson and Gerhardsson reported on lead intoxication from ingested lead shot retained in the gastrointestinal tract, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2005. 43. Kosnett reviewed the health effects of low-dose lead exposure in adults and children, emphasizing the risks from consuming game meat harvested with lead ammunition. 44. Panariti and Berxholi documented lead toxicity in humans from contaminated flour in Albania, published in Veterinary and Human Toxicology in 1998. 45. El-Sharif et al. reported on the re-emergence of lead poisoning from contaminated flour in a Palestinian village, published in the International Journal of Occupational and Environmental Health in 2000. 46. Kákosy et al. described an epidemic of lead intoxication caused by contaminated ground paprika, published in Clinical Toxicology in 1996. 47. Hore et al. reviewed spices as a potential source of lead exposure over a 10-year period, published in the Journal of Public Health Management and Practice in 2019. 48. Al Khayat et al. reported on acute lead encephalopathy in early infancy, published in Annals of Tropical Paediatrics in 1997. 49. Karri et al. described lead encephalopathy due to traditional medicines, published in Current Drug Safety in 2008. 50. Ritchy et al. documented lead poisoning among Burmese refugee children in Indiana, published in Clinical Pediatrics in 2011. 51. Breeher et al. reported a cluster of lead poisoning cases among consumers of Ayurvedic medicine, published in the International Journal of Occupational and Environmental Health in 2015. 52. Ying et al. described childhood lead poisoning from folk prescriptions for treating rhinitis, published in BMC Pediatrics in 2018. 53. Lynch and Braithwaite reviewed the clinical and toxicological aspects of herbal medicines adulterated with heavy metals, published in Expert Opinion on Drug Safety in 2005. 54. Mathee et al. investigated a lead poisoning outbreak from Ayurvedic medicine consumption in Durban, South Africa, published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2015. 55. Van Schalkwyk et al. reported on plumbism cases associated with Ayurvedic medicine, published in the New Zealand Medical Journal in 2006. 56. Mehta et al. described lead intoxication due to Ayurvedic medications as a cause of abdominal pain in adults, published in Clinical Toxicology in 2017. 57. Ying et al. reported on pediatric lead poisoning from folk prescriptions for treating epilepsy, published in Clinica Chimica Acta in 2016. 58. Dargan et al. reviewed heavy metal poisoning from Ayurvedic traditional medicines, published in the International Journal of Environmental Health in 2008. 59. Al-Ashban et al. studied the toxic effects of kohl, a traditional eye cosmetic, in Saudi Arabia, published in Public Health in 2004. 60. Lin et al. investigated pediatric lead exposure from imported Indian spices and cultural powders, published in Pediatrics in 2010. 61. Schwarcz et al. documented childhood lead exposure associated with the use of kajal, an eye cosmetic from Afghanistan, published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2013. 62. Mowad et al. reported on the management of lead poisoning from ingested fishing sinkers, published in Archives of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine in 1998. 63. Van Arsdale et al. described lead poisoning from a toy necklace, published in Pediatrics in 2004. 64. Newton et al. reported on lead poisoning from a lead weight, published in Annals of Clinical Biochemistry in 2005. 65. McNutt et al. documented lead poisoning after ingestion of 206 lead bullets, published in Veterinary and Human Toxicology in 2001. 66. Phipps et al. described lead poisoning due to geophagia, specifically the consumption of miniature pottery, published in the Open Journal of Pediatrics in 2012. 67. Goyer reviewed lead toxicity in the fifth edition of Patty’s Toxicology, providing a comprehensive overview of lead’s effects on human health. 68. The CDC reported on adult blood lead epidemiology and surveillance in the United States for 2008–2009, published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2011. 69. Kondrashov et al. assessed lead exposure risk in locksmiths, published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2005. 70. Laidlaw et al. reviewed lead exposure at firing ranges, published in Environmental Health in 2017. 71. Hipkins et al. reported on family lead poisoning associated with occupational exposure, published in Clinical Pediatrics. 72. The CDC documented lead poisoning associated with intravenous methamphetamine use in Oregon, published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 1989. 73. Busse et al. reported on lead poisoning due to adulterated marijuana, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2008. 74. Ghane et al. described a lead poisoning outbreak among opium users in Iran, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2018. 75. Kokori et al. reported on an anemic infant in a coma due to lead poisoning, published in The Lancet in 1998. 76. Dargan et al. described a case of lead poisoning due to snooker chalk, published in Archives of Disease in Childhood in 2000. 77. Sabouraud et al. reported on lead poisoning following ingestion of lead roofing plates, published in Clinical Toxicology in 2008. 78. Manton and Malloy studied the distribution of lead in body fluids after ingestion of soft solder, published in the British Journal of Industrial Medicine in 1983. 79. Shannon reported on severe lead poisoning during pregnancy, published in Ambulatory Pediatrics in 2003. 80. Grasso et al. described systemic lead toxicity from retained shrapnel, presenting as jaundice and hepatitis, published in Military Medicine in 2017. 81. Karpatkin reported on lead poisoning after ingestion of lead acetate with suicidal intent, published in Archives of Environmental Health in 1961. 82. Nortier et al. described acute lead poisoning with hemolysis and liver toxicity after ingestion of red lead, published in Veterinary and Human Toxicology in 1980. 83. Pelclová et al. questioned whether Central Europe is safe from environmental lead intoxications, published in the Central European Journal of Public Health in 2016. 84. Sixel-Dietrich et al. reported on acute lead intoxication due to intravenous injection, published in Human Toxicology in 1985. 85. Kordas explored dietary approaches to prevent or treat lead exposure, published in the Journal of Pediatrics in 2017. 86. Vork et al. estimated workplace air and worker blood lead concentrations using an updated physiologically-based pharmacokinetic model, accessed on August 31, 2021. 87. The Toxicological Profile for Lead provides a detailed analysis of lead’s toxicological properties and health effects, accessed on August 31, 2021. 88. Apte et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on lead toxicity from retained bullet fragments, published in the Journal of Trauma.
